title: The mountain again (Mark 9:1–13)
hookLine: the transfiguration, then down the mountain into need

cards: Some moments you want to bottle. A wedding night. A retreat.
A concert where everyone sang the last chorus together. Going home feels wrong. Today three fishermen get a moment like that, and a far stranger one.

Six days after the hard talk about the cross, Jesus leads Peter, James and John up a high mountain, alone. In Mark, mountains are where things happen: he went up one to pray, and up one to call the twelve.
This time something happens to him. And then they have to walk back down.

teach.b: First, the change. Mark says he was transfigured before them, his clothes shining white, whiter than any cloth-bleacher on earth could make them. A detail about laundry, right next to the glory of God.
Elijah and Moses appear, talking with Jesus. Tradition hears the Law in Moses and the prophets in Elijah: the story of Israel, on one mountaintop with him. Third, Peter.
He blurts out, in the Douay-Rheims: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles." Tents. Stay.
Keep it. Mark adds, kindly, that Peter didn't know what to say; they were terrified. Then a cloud covers them, and a voice: "This is my most beloved son; hear ye him."
Not build him a tent. Listen. Suddenly, looking around, they see no one but Jesus only.
Fourth, the way down. On the path he tells them to tell no one until the Son of man has risen from the dead, and they argue about what rising from the dead could even mean.
They ask about Elijah, and he says Elijah has already come.

teach.h: THIS IS MY MOST BELOVED SON; HEAR YE HIM.
teach.b: Mark doesn't name him; in Matthew's telling, the disciples understand he means John the Baptist. Mark lets no one stay on the mountain. At the bottom, tomorrow, a crowd and a desperate father are already waiting.

how: Catholics celebrate the Feast of the Transfiguration on August 6, and the story is read every year on the Second Sunday of Lent, as a glimpse of glory before the road to the cross.

o: changed in appearance, shining with glory
shown in a dream, not seen in waking life
moved from one place to another in an instant

games.q: who's on the mountain — tap the pairs.
p: the one who gave the Law

s: Mark says Jesus's clothes became whiter than any bleacher could make them
a down-to-earth detail beside the glory: whiter than any cloth-bleacher on earth.
the voice from the cloud tells them to build the tents
the voice says "hear ye him." listen, not build.
the disciples stay on the mountain for days
they come straight back down, and a crowd is waiting at the bottom.

games.q: you're Peter on the mountain. Jesus is shining, Moses and Elijah are there, and you're terrified. what do you say?
o: let's build three tents and stay.
let's go and tell everyone right now.
games.why: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles." Mark says he didn't know what to say. then the cloud, and the voice: hear him.

practice: Sit for a minute and rest: if you pray, in whatever prayer you have, or in the words hear ye him; if you don't, in the quiet, like a view from a high place.
Then walk down the mountain in your mind and see who's at the bottom today, someone who needs a call, a ride, a meal, an apology. Pick one person, and the one thing you'll do.

wordCard.voice: Transfigured. What happened to Jesus before Peter, James and John on the mountain: his clothes shining white, Moses and Elijah beside him, and a voice saying hear him. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: he was transfigured, from the same root as metamorphosis.

carryVoice: Your line: down the mountain. The voice said listen, not stay. Day two hundred fifteen, done.
